\begin{equation} \Phi _F(A_0,t)=e^{-\int _{t_0}^{t}R_{\min }(s)/2\, ds} \left[A_0-2\pi \int _{t_0}^{t} e^{\int _{t_0}^{s}R_{\min }(v)/2\, dv}\, ds\right], \quad R_{\min }(s)=\inf _{x\in M}R(x,s). \end{equation} It satisfies $\Phi _F(A_0,t_0)=A_0$ and $\partial _t\Phi _F=-2\pi -R_{\min }(t)\Phi _F/2$ on the closed slab. Differences of initial values are multiplied by the positive exponential factor, so initial area errors transfer quantitatively to terminal errors.

Theorem
[Deformation of a null loop family]
